text: Git branching is an important part of modern version control. A branch lets you work on new features without affecting the main code. Developers often create feature branches to build and test new ideas safely. When the work is finished, the branch can be merged back into the main project. Many teams use pull requests to review changes before merging, which helps catch mistakes early. This workflow keeps the project organized and allows several people to work at the same time. By using branches, merging, and pull requests together, teams can develop software faster and with fewer problems.
